title: INSTITUTE OF FORENSIC SCIENCE
body_text:
The Government has set up the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) under the Act of the Parliament in the year 2020 as an Institution of National Importance to facilitate and promote studies and research and to achieve excellence in the field of forensic science in conjunction with applied behavioural science studies, law, criminology and other allied areas and technology and other related fields.
Apart from the initial campuses of the NFSU in Gandhinagar (Gujarat) and Delhi, approval has been given for setting up of 14 additional campuses of the NFSU in Goa, Agartala (Tripura), Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh), Dharwad (Karnataka), Guwahati (Assam), Nagpur (Maharashtra), Khordha (Odisha), Raipur (Chhattisgarh), Chengalpattu (Tamil Nadu), Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh. The NFSU has also set up training academies in Imphal (Manipur) and Pune (Maharashtra).
This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Lok Sabha that the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU), established by an Act of Parliament in 2020 as an Institution of National Importance, initially had campuses in Gandhinagar (Gujarat) and Delhi. The government has since approved 14 additional NFSU campuses across states including Goa, Tripura, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Assam, Maharashtra, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh. NFSU has also set up training academies in Imphal (Manipur) and Pune (Maharashtra).
enrichment.context: The NFSU was created to build specialized human resources and research capacity in forensic science, applied behavioural science, criminology, and law, addressing India's chronic shortage of trained forensic experts and forensic infrastructure needed for evidence-based criminal investigation and prosecution. Its expansion assumes greater significance in light of the new criminal laws—the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam—which mandate forensic investigation for offences carrying punishment of seven years or more, creating a large demand for forensic scientists, DNA analysts, and cyber-forensic experts across states. The push to decentralize NFSU campuses reflects a broader governance strategy to strengthen state-level forensic science laboratories (FSLs), reduce case backlogs, and improve conviction rates through scientific evidence rather than reliance on witness testimony or confessions alone. This move is also linked to the Nirbhaya Fund-supported initiatives for setting up FSLs and DNA testing facilities in various states following recommendations after the 2012 Delhi gang-rape case, and it complements the National Policy on Criminal Justice reforms aimed at modernizing India's investigative and judicial ecosystem.

prelims_questions.question: With reference to the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU), consider the following statements: 1. It was established as an Institution of National Importance by an Act of Parliament in 2020. 2. Its original campuses are located in Gandhinagar and Delhi. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the NFSU was established under an Act of Parliament in 2020 as an Institution of National Importance, with its initial campuses located in Gandhinagar (Gujarat) and Delhi. Both statements are correct.

prelims_questions.question: NFSU training academies, as mentioned in a recent Lok Sabha reply, have been set up in which of the following pairs of locations?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that NFSU has set up training academies specifically in Imphal (Manipur) and Pune (Maharashtra), distinct from the additional degree-granting campuses in other states.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of forensic science in strengthening India's criminal justice system in the context of the new criminal law framework (BNS, BNSS, BSA). How does the expansion of institutions like the National Forensic Sciences University address existing gaps?

mains_questions.question: Institutions of National Importance play a critical role in specialized higher education and capacity building in India. Examine this in the context of the National Forensic Sciences University and its recent expansion across states.
